thread:
sylvie: Pulled yesterday's nsys from the nightly matmul job — there's a ~120ms stall inside the 'algo selection' path right after a KV-cache miss. uploaded trace: https://internal-artifacts/snapshots/2412345600.ns.zip

devin: I skimmed it. Looks like cublasLt picks an algo that needs a huge workspace for one shape, then we spin on allocator/launch. timeline shows repeated cudaMallocAsync attempts + kernel launches queued behind allocation.

mike: can you paste the nsys summary snippet? curious whether it's allocator fragmentation or the algo probe loop itself causing the stall.

sylvie: here's the hotlist from nsys (trimmed):
```
cublasLtMatmulAlgoSelection    122.4ms  (hot)
cudaMallocAsync                46.1ms
kernel: matmul_prelaunch        8.3ms
kernel: matmul_exec            10.2ms
cudaDeviceSynchronize          2.0ms
```
Seems the selection call itself spins while allocating a workspace, then we do a few small launches, then fallback path in runtime triggers additional allocs.

devin: that aligns with the 'workspace spike -> fragmentation -> preemption' hypothesis. Also check whether KV cache miss path is forcing a different seq-len and thus different algo probe. Could be shape/seq-length mismatch between warm cache and cold cache.

mike: perf-bot alerted on this yesterday — nightly delta: +9.4% p99 for matmul-heavy endpoints. perf-bot: "matmul-regression-241234"

perf-bot: nightly job matmul-regression: regression detected (+9.4% p99). Trace attached to thread.

devin: quick repro: run the nightly matmul benchmark with env overrides to force deterministic algo:
```bash
CUBLASLT_ALGO_CONFIG=force_algo_17 ./tools/run_matmul_bench --shape 1x4096x4096 --reps 200 --warmup 50
```
If the stall disappears, it's the heuristics/algo probe causing the allocs. If not, it's allocator behavior.

sylvie: i'll run that now on a dev box and also try clamping workspace with our runtime flag (--max-cublas-workspace=64MB) to see if that prevents the big cudaMallocAsync.

mike: also try running with sampler trace (perfetto) on a cold start to capture the KV miss timing relative to algo probe. I suspect the KV cache miss increases seq len briefly which flips the algo table.

devin: small follow-up: if it is cublasLt returning an unsupported algo and we fall back to cublasGemm, the fallback path currently does lazy allocations that race with other requests — that can amplify a single large workspace into a transient fragmentation storm. We should: 1) record the requested workspace size in traces, 2) limit the probe to preferred-algo set when under mem-pressure.

sylvie: thumbs up. i'll attach logs from the repro runs here once done. planning two quick patches if repro confirms: a) clamp workspace for probe-only phase, b) surface requested_workspace_bytes in the runtime telemetry so we can alert on spikes.

mike: thanks — if you need me to flip a Dedicated pool to repro on the same HW, ping me.

sylvie: thanks all, starting runs now. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
